findings.text: Steal time for a CPU lives in per CPU storage and is reported in nanoseconds. Wide builds use one ordered read. Narrow builds read the high half twice around the low half with ordering separation, retry while the high pair disagrees, then combine halves. The counter is scaled with a hypervisor supplied multiplier and shift.

Steal registration follows an availability flag. Guest init registers the current CPU area and logs identity and physical location. Disable releases the registration. A reboot notifier block invokes disable on every CPU for restart. Boot preparation chains guest init before native preparation. Hotplug online registers and down prepare disables.
Hotplug online and down prepare for steal time mask local interrupts across the registration or teardown work and restore interrupt state on completion with a success result.
Early boot enables the paravirtual steal static keys when steal time is available, with runqueue accounting enabled only when its accounting flag is set, then reports success.

Paravirtual setup names the platform and disables delay handling. Without known TSC frequency it stops. Otherwise it prepares cycle conversion, installs scheduler clock when present, and on steal availability marks steal usable, installs the steal callback, registers the reboot notifier, and on multiprocessor builds wires boot and hotplug hooks or initializes directly on uniprocessor builds.
Scheduler clock installation replaces the static call target with the caller supplied callback.
Builds without paravirtual clock support provide empty scheduler clock setter and empty VMware setup operations with no observable effect.

VMware capability setup always forces constant and reliable timestamp features, forces known frequency when hypervisor frequency is known, and forces exactly one of the two hypercall mechanism features according to negotiated mode.

Platform setup covers hypervisor frequency discovery, kilohertz and delay calibration derivation, calibration hook installation, bus and APIC period recording with informational logging, table discovery adjustment for confidential guests without EFI boot, paravirtual setup, timer verification suppression, and forced capabilities. Frequency failure yields only a warning.

Hypercall selection summarizes the two mechanism bits from the feature leaf. Detection requires the hypervisor CPU feature plus a twelve byte vendor signature match with mode recording and logging, otherwise a serial based system match plus legacy probe is used. No match reports absence.
Legacy extended APIC availability comes from a vCPU information query and is true only when a reserved indicator is clear while a legacy indicator is set.

Confidential hypercall wrapper rejects non VMware use and out of mask commands with a one time warning and maximum unsigned return. Valid calls marshal inputs plus vendor leaf, function, magic, command and zero privilege level, invoke the low level call, fill up to five optional outputs where callers supply storage, and return the result field.

Encrypted guest hypercall exchange uses a communication block. Preparation copies instruction pointer plus five data registers into the block. Completion requires all six registers valid, then copies them back and reports success, otherwise reports failure without state change.
VMware hypervisor descriptor carries display name, detection and type identity, platform init and extended APIC hooks, plus encrypted guest prepare and finish hooks when memory encryption is built.

Vortex processor descriptor carries vendor and system on chip identity plus vendor number. Legacy naming covers family five models for DX and MX variants and family six model zero for the EX variant, where a newer revision is distinguished by product name query support.

Zhaoxin feature control uses MSR hexadecimal 1257. Presence and enabled indicators use bit six and seven for crypto and bit two and three for random number. Enable controls use bit seven for crypto and bit eight for random number.

Zhaoxin init is gated on extended CPUID range. Present but disabled crypto and random units are enabled through the feature MSR with logging. Extended flags become capability word five. Repeat, constant and nonstop timestamp, performance monitoring under version and counter thresholds, and fence behavior are set by family, power, level and build, with cache and feature control delegated to shared helpers.

Zhaoxin processor descriptor carries lower case vendor label and Shanghai identity plus vendor number, with early and full init hooks and on 32 bit builds a cache size hook returning its input unchanged.
Cross CPU CPUID work pairs a register snapshot for input leaf and output values with a completion primitive. The remote helper executes the counted query on the target CPU then signals completion.

CPUID reads require sixteen byte multiples and reject other sizes. Each unit targets the CPU from the file minor, splits file position into leaf and subleaf, waits for remote completion, copies sixteen bytes to user space, advances position by one leaf and rearms completion. Dispatch or copy failure ends the transfer. Open rejects out of range or offline CPUs and CPUs without CPUID.

CPUID driver exposes per CPU character devices with open, read and end oriented seek behavior under a dedicated class with CPU numbered nodes. Hotplug transitions create and destroy devices. Init and exit register and unregister the character range, class and hotplug state with cleanup on failure.
Crash map helper carries a boot parameter pointer alongside a memory type used when building firmware memory entries.

Kdump NMI handling per CPU saves register state, halts processor tracing, runs a confidential callback and disables the local APIC. The shootdown entry broadcasts that handler then disables the APIC on the initiator as well.

Crash shootdown disables interrupts, warns and ignores reentry, records the initiator, publishes caller callback and pending count, installs a preemptive emergency handler, broadcasts to others, publishes an issued flag, then polls up to about one second while retaining the handler for late responders. The uniprocessor variant does nothing.
Emergency handler install warns on reinstalling the same handler, stores the new handler, then issues a write barrier so other CPUs observe it before return.

Crash range sizing starts from three plus a contiguous allocation count to allow splits, then walks RAM to count. Low one megabyte is always excluded. Population copies each RAM resource bounds into the crash table in walk order.

Firmware table insertion fails when the zero page table is full, otherwise appends and counts the entry. Resource mapping builds address, span size and supplied type. Exclusion starts from a caller range then removes the executable header area and when present the disk key area.

Reentering shootdown risks handler list corruption and callback mutation, so it is warned and ignored. Clearing the callback after timeout risks failure on late arrival, so the callback stays installed.
Narrow steal reads without paired high validation risk torn time values. Firmware table overflow silently truncates entries beyond capacity.
Crash logging in this file prefixes messages with the word kexec plus colon and space.
